# A tree list moves an item into another folder by drag

## Context

#21140's target gives the Trees group one card at the Engine 14 cut, a file explorer whose "items move by drag" (row Trees). Checked on 19 Nov (#21140 `issuecomment-7006670970`): the engine cannot do that today, so the card waits on this ticket and on its sibling for rename in place.

unowned-rationale: an engine feature the Trees card needs; a maintainer takes it when the band's examples are in review, and if it misses the lock (Sun 22 Nov 18:00 CET) the card rides the next cut.

## The Problem

`Neo.tree.List` accepts `dragResortable: true`, which creates a `Neo.draggable.tree.SortZone` (`src/tree/List.mjs`, `afterSetDragResortable`). That class adds nothing to `Neo.draggable.tree.DragZone`: `src/draggable/tree/SortZone.mjs` is a 22-line subclass with only `className` and `ntype`, and `DragZone.mjs` (100 lines) marks draggable items and renders the proxy but has no drop logic. A visitor who drags a file onto a folder sees the proxy, and the item stays where it was.

## The Architectural Reality

- `Neo.tree.List` renders a flat store of records with `parentId`, `isLeaf` and `collapsed` (`createItems`, `createItemLevel`); `onStoreRecordChange` updates it when a record changes.
- `Neo.draggable.list.SortZone` and `Neo.draggable.container.SortZone` are the sibling drop implementations: index computation from item rects, a move on drop, and the `currentIndex`/cancel paths that #20849 hardened.
- `Neo.draggable.tree.DragZone` keeps `leafNodesOnly` and the drag-out-to-drop-zone path that `examples/tree` uses (`draggable: true`); `dragResortable` and `draggable` are mutually exclusive by design.

## The Fix

Give `Neo.draggable.tree.SortZone` its drop logic. While a drag moves over the tree, the target is a gap before or after a sibling, or a folder, shown in place. On drop, update the record's `parentId` and its position among the new siblings, and let the list render from the store. A folder cannot move into itself or a descendant.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1: A leaf dragged onto another folder ends up in it: its record's `parentId` is the folder's id, and the tree shows it there.
- [ ] AC-2: A leaf dragged between two siblings lands between them, in the same folder or another.
- [ ] AC-3: A folder dragged onto its own descendant is refused, and the tree is unchanged.
- [ ] AC-4: A component spec covers AC-1 to AC-3 with real pointer drags; `examples/tree`'s drag into its drop zone (`draggable: true`) keeps working.

## Out of Scope

- Dragging between two trees, or into another window.
- Keyboard moves.
- Rename in place: its own ticket.
- Opening a closed folder while a drag hovers it. A drop onto a closed folder already moves the item into it; opening on hover needs a public way to open a folder on `Neo.tree.List`, which keyboard moves would share. (Moved here at intake, 19 Nov.)
